title: polytypo locale data
description: Declarative typographic conventions for one locale. Literal strings, literal code points, string lists and enum values only — no patterns, no priorities, no expressions (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.1).

locale.description: BCP-47 language or language-region tag. Must equal the file name.

name.description: English name of the locale, for generated documentation.

parenthetical.description: Dash used for a parenthetical break. `-tight` means no surrounding spaces, `-spaced` means a regular space on each side (the leading one may later be made non-breaking by the nbsp rule). `none` means the locale has no verified convention and the rule must not substitute anything.

range.description: Dash used between numbers and dates. Russian sets an em dash here. `none` means the locale has no verified convention and the rule must not substitute anything — a missing citation is never a licence to guess.

abbreviatedAfterTerminal.description: When true, an ellipsis directly after `!` or `?` is written with two dots (`?..`) rather than three. Russian convention.

hyphen.description: Morphological forms whose hyphen must not break across lines. Empty arrays are the normal case — only a few languages have a normative list.

prefixes.description: Word-initial forms written with a trailing hyphen, e.g. Russian "кое-".

suffixes.description: Word-final forms written with a leading hyphen, e.g. Russian "-таки".

compounds.description: Whole hyphenated forms, written with U+002D, e.g. Russian "из-под".

beforePunctuation.description: Characters that take U+00A0 before them.

narrowBeforePunctuation.description: Characters that take U+202F before them.

afterShortWords.description: Lowercase words that must not be left at the end of a line; the space after them becomes U+00A0. Matching is case-insensitive only for the first character.

abbreviations.description: Literal multi-token abbreviations written with regular U+0020; every internal space becomes U+00A0. Example: "z. B.".

beforeUnits.description: Units and signs that bind to a preceding number with U+00A0. Example: "%", "km", "°C".

beforeNumber.description: Abbreviations that bind to a following number with U+00A0. Example: "Nr.", "S.", "art.".

beforeWord.description: Abbreviations that bind to a following word with U+00A0. Example: "г.", "ул.", "M.", "Mme". Riskier than beforeNumber — list only forms whose binding is normative.

afterSymbols.description: Symbols that bind to a following number with U+00A0. Example: "§", "№".

bindInitials.description: When true, initials are bound to each other and to the surname with U+00A0.

rule.description: Which rule the citation is normative for. Values are rule ids from spec/rules/order.json — note the rule is `dashes` while the locale-data field it reads is `dash`.

cite.description: Normative authority, named precisely enough to be looked up offline.

sources.description: Mandatory. Every locale-driven rule with non-default data must be covered by at least one citation (docs/PLAN.md section 6.1).

innerSpace.description: Space inserted between the quotation mark and the quoted text, as in French guillemets.

singleChar.description: Exactly one Unicode code point, written as the literal character. maxLength is 2 only because a JSON validator counts UTF-16 units; the one-code-point rule is enforced by scripts/validate-spec.mjs, which is the portable check. U+0022 and U+0027 are forbidden: the quotes rule reasons about straight marks as input and would not terminate if a locale declared one as output.
